versions.name: RXV2-0.9.871-release-number-always-sent
versions.notes: Telemetry items 39 and 40 (the release number, and the transmitter-ordered update) were skipped whenever no phone had set the clock this boot: the rotation went from item 37 straight back to 0. Now sent every time. Found on the bench: the transmitter said 'The receiver did not say its version' as soon as the receiver was power-cycled.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.870-one-update-at-a-time
versions.notes: One update at a time: an install asked for over WiFi, or ordered by the transmitter, is refused while the app is writing firmware over Bluetooth (a WiFi install cut a Bluetooth transfer short at 442 KB on the bench); a second Bluetooth 'begin' while the first still streams is refused too.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.869-installable-from-the-transmitter
versions.notes: Same firmware as 0.9.868: something for a receiver on 0.9.868 to install from the transmitter.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.868-release-list-read-as-written
versions.notes: Transmitter-ordered update: the release list is read as the website writes it (a space after every colon); 0.9.864-867 expected none and would have reported 'release not in the list'.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.867-install-time-logged
versions.notes: The event log says how long an install took (firmware and pages, in seconds), so the transmitter's silence during a transmitter-ordered update can be sized from real numbers.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.866-quiet-radio-for-the-download
versions.notes: Transmitter-ordered update: Bluetooth is switched off again just before the download (the WiFi start had brought it back up), so the download runs on a quiet radio.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.865-installable-from-the-transmitter
versions.notes: Same firmware as 0.9.864, released so that a receiver on 0.9.864 has something to install from the transmitter: the first release to be installed that way. Receivers older than 0.9.864 still need one update from the phone app (they cannot say their version to the transmitter yet).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.864-update-from-the-transmitter
versions.notes: A V1B transmitter can now update the receiver: with a model connected, the transmitter's Check for update compares this receiver's release number (telemetry item 39) with messiter.com and, on Install, orders the update over the radio (parameter 35). The receiver accepts only disarmed and knowing a WiFi network, acts only once the transmitter has gone quiet, joins the network it already knows, installs the exact version ordered with the same code the app uses, and restarts; item 40 tells the transmitter how it went. No password ever travels over the air. state.json shows tx_update.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.863-flights-kept-gaps-honest
versions.notes: Flights: a save that could not start is retried or logged, never silently lost; gaps while disarmed are left out of the link statistics (a real in-flight loss still counts); both apps record flight data first and re-check the list at the end, so a short post-landing connection keeps the flights for review

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.862-per-cell-average
versions.notes: Battery card reads '3.8 V per cell (average)'

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.861-install-request-is-judged
versions.notes: Update page: the install request is awaited and judged (a lost request said 'stopped at the end' after minutes); the bar moves only once the install is under way; twenty seconds of normal answers = 'not started, try again'; 'Update now' from the front page lands on the WiFi/Bluetooth choice instead of picking a lane; the receiver logs every install request

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.860-save-bar-steps-aside
versions.notes: Save to Flight Controller bar: steps aside while the keyboard is up (it used to chase the scroll and jump); tap the keypad's tick and it is back

rotorflight.line: Rotorflight 2.3 — the release these pages are written and tested against.
